column3:
An 8 ft 2.75 2-way post boxed with its press cap, 7 L-brackets, a bottom spacer with screws and a cover strip for the blank side, for the post where an aluminum slat fence run stops.

What the aluminum fence end post kit does

The (Fence Box) 2.75 2-way End Post Kit 8 ft from Aluglobus Aluminum Systems is an aluminum fence end post kit for the point where a slat fence run stops: against a wall, beside a gate opening or at the end of a property line. It is built on the same 2.75 2-way post used along the rest of the run, boxed with the hardware to fix slats and rails on the working side and a cover strip to close off the side that has nothing attached.

The post is extruded from 6063-T6 aluminum and finished with AAMA 2604 super-durable powder coating. The price list marks the kit MADE IN USA and gives its usage as pedestrian gates, fence and wall topper.

What's in the box

2-way Post1pc
2-way Post Press cap1pc
L-Brackets (for securing slats and rails)7pcs
1" or 2" Spacer with screw bush (bottom spacer)1pc
#12×2" Self-Tapping screws, Black (for the bottom spacer)2pcs
Cover Strip, Black (post cover on the blank side)1 pc

Compare that with the standard (Fence Box) 2.75 2-way Post Kit 8 ft, which is packed with 14 L-brackets, 4 bottom spacers and 8 screws and has no cover strip. The end kit carries 7 L-brackets, 1 bottom spacer and 2 screws, plus the cover strip, because only one side of the post holds slats.

End post or line post: which one you need

A 2.75 2-way post is designed to take slat panels on two opposite sides, which is exactly what you want in the middle of a run. At the end of a run, one of those sides is left empty. This kit gives that post a finished face by covering the blank side instead of leaving an open channel on show.

  • End post kit: where a run finishes and only one side of the post carries slats.
  • Standard 2-way post kit: for each post that has panels on both sides.
  • Corners, hinge and latch posts: confirm the correct post with our team before ordering.

Note that the price list gives the end kit's usage as pedestrian gates, fence and wall topper, while the standard 2-way post kit also lists sliding gates. If your end post will sit next to a sliding gate, check the setup with us first.

Colors and availability

The 2.75 2-way end post is listed in Black, Bronze and White. In the kit inclusions, the cover strip and the #12×2" self-tapping screws are listed as Black for every color. If an exact color match on the blank side matters on a Bronze or White fence, ask our team before you order.

This kit belongs to the Oct / Nov Gen 3.0 Fence Box release, and some colors may be listed as coming soon. Confirm current stock for your color before you set an install date or book a crew.

Planning your fence run

Sketch the layout first. Mark where every run starts and stops, then count end posts and line posts separately so each position gets the right kit. Check your opening widths and post spacing against your slat length before ordering, and follow the included instructions and your local code for footings or surface mounting.

The kit does not include slats, slat spacers or mounting hardware. For slab or wall mounting, the 2.75 2-way post baseplate is sold separately. If you are starting from scratch, a complete Alu 40 8ft x 6ft 2-way post fence kit bundles slats, a post kit and spacers in one order, and you can add an end post kit for the last post of each run. Browse the full range of aluminum fence kits and parts to match slats and accessories to your end posts.

If you are unsure how many end posts your layout needs, send us a sketch with your run lengths and gate positions, and our team will help you check the parts list before you order.

The L-brackets secure slats and rails to the post, and the bottom spacers with their self-tapping screws sit at the base of the post. The press cap closes the top. Check the exact contents against the included instructions when you unbox.

Buying the post kit on its own lets you add extra sections, replace a post, or build a run to your own layout without paying for slats you already have.

  • Between two panels: use this aluminum slat fence post kit.
  • At the end of a run: use the 2.75 2-way end post kit, which adds a cover strip for the blank side.
  • At a gate: the pedestrian gate post options list the 2.75 2-way post for wall mount only, for gates up to 3 feet wide. For wider or free-standing gates, ask our team about square post options.

Slat spacers are not in the box. They set the gap between slats inside the 2-way post and are sold in Gen 3.0 packs:

  • (Pack of 30pcs) 3/8 in. spacers for a 3/8 gap
  • (Pack of 30pcs) 1/2 in. spacers for a 1/2 gap

Check the minimum gap listed for your slat before you choose. The price list notes a minimum gap of 3/8 in. for the boxed Alu 40 8 ft slats, for example.

Measure your runs, mark every post position and decide which positions need a line post and which need an end post. Precise spacing for straight, balanced fence runs

The 3/8″ aluminum spacer is a small but essential component in modern fencing systems. It provides the precision needed to maintain consistent spacing between fence boards or slats, ensuring your installation looks straight, balanced, and professional.

Whether you’re building a privacy fence, decorative screen, or pool enclosure, using spacers eliminates guesswork and prevents uneven gaps. This results in a fence that not only looks better but also performs longer, as evenly spaced panels distribute stress more effectively.

Homeowners and contractors in Los Angeles, Beverly Hills, Orange County, and nationwide trust our 6063-T6 aluminum spacers for their durability and ease of use. Unlike plastic spacers, which can crack, or steel alternatives, which rust, these aluminum spacers deliver years of reliable service with zero maintenance.

Aluminum vs plastic vs steel

The 3/8 Spacer outperforms plastic spacers that crack or compress over time, and steel spacers that rust and corrode. Its 6063-T6 aluminum construction maintains precise dimensions under pressure and in all weather conditions, delivering a fence that looks professionally installed from day one and stays that way for decades.

Perfect for contractors seeking consistent results and DIY homeowners wanting flawless spacing, the 3/8 Spacer is the reliable choice for any modern fencing project.

FAQ

Frequently Asked Questions

How many 3/8 spacers do I need per fence panel?

Typically, you’ll need 2–4 spacers per panel, depending on the design and length of the section.

Can I paint the spacer to match my fence color?

Yes. While our spacers are powder-coated in standard black, they are also available in custom colors upon request.

Are aluminum spacers better for pool fences?

Yes. Aluminum spacers are non-rusting, UV-resistant, and code-compliant, making them an excellent choice for pool enclosures.

Do spacers affect the strength of the fence?

Yes, in a positive way. Spacers ensure panels are evenly aligned, which distributes stress more evenly and helps the fence remain stable over time.

Unlike generic plastic spacers, our 6063-T6 aluminum spacers are contractor-grade, built to last decades, and available with nationwide shipping.

Step by step

Installation Process

Installing the CLAD120 black aluminum wall cladding is straightforward, whether you’re a professional contractor or a confident DIY enthusiast. The interlocking panel system is engineered for a precise fit, long-term durability, and a clean, modern look on any surface.

01

Prepare the Surface

A smooth, stable surface is the foundation of a long-lasting cladding installation. Begin by checking that your wall, frame, or supporting structure is level, completely dry, and strong enough to hold the panels securely. Any existing loose paint, rust, or debris should be removed to prevent uneven mounting and moisture entrapment. For metal frames, ensure all welds are smooth and there are no sharp edges that could damage the panel coating. A clean, prepared surface not only makes installation easier but also improves the cladding’s resistance to wind uplift and weather damage over time.

02

Plan the Layout

Accurate planning is critical for a professional finish. Use a measuring tape and level to mark out straight guidelines across the installation area before fixing any panels. This ensures consistent alignment from the very first piece to the last. If you are installing vertically, draw plumb lines every few feet to maintain precision. For horizontal cladding, mark parallel lines at regular intervals. This planning phase is also when you determine where joints, corner trims, or special cuts will be made, helping reduce waste and giving the final project a balanced, symmetrical appearance.

03

Install a Starter Strip

The starter strip (or starter rail) is the anchor of your entire cladding system. Position it along the bottom edge for horizontal installations, or on the side for vertical applications, making sure it is perfectly level. Secure it with corrosion-resistant screws or rivets, spaced evenly to prevent movement under load. The starter strip locks the first panel in place and dictates the alignment of every subsequent panel, so take the time to ensure it’s positioned accurately. Poor placement at this stage will result in visible misalignment across the whole project.

04

Fit the First Panel

Place the first CLAD120 black aluminum panel into the starter strip, pressing firmly to engage the interlocking profile. Fasten the panel using stainless steel or galvanized screws, ensuring they penetrate into a solid substrate or supporting framework. Avoid overtightening, which can distort the panel or scratch the powder coating. This first panel serves as the baseline for the entire run, so double-check its position with a level before moving forward. Correcting mistakes is far easier at this stage than once several panels are installed.

05

Continue Interlocking

Slide each new panel into the groove of the previous one, using the built-in Lego-style interlocking system to create a seamless, weather-tight connection. Check alignment after every two to three panels to ensure the line remains straight. This system naturally conceals fasteners, giving the cladding a clean, modern look. For large installations, consider working in sections to keep panels manageable and reduce alignment errors over long runs. The interlocking design not only improves aesthetics but also increases structural integrity by distributing load evenly across the cladding.

06

Trim and Finish

Measure and cut panels to fit at edges, corners, or around openings using a miter saw fitted with a non-ferrous metal blade. This ensures clean, accurate cuts without damaging the coating. Install finishing trims such as L-shaped corner profiles, U-channel edge caps, or matching fascia strips to protect exposed edges from moisture and impact damage. These finishing pieces also give the installation a polished, high-end appearance. If cladding around gates, pergolas, or other outdoor structures, ensure all trims are securely fastened to withstand wind and movement.

07

Inspect for Alignment

Once installation is complete, conduct a thorough inspection. Verify that all panels are perfectly aligned, with no visible gaps or misaligned joints. Check that fasteners are secure, trims are firmly attached, and there is no panel movement under light pressure. A well-installed CLAD120 black aluminum cladding system should remain straight, stable, and maintenance-free for years, providing exceptional resistance to UV fading, corrosion, and weather-related damage. This method works equally well for exterior facades, privacy walls, aluminum fences, driveway gates, and modern pergola designs, making it one of the most versatile cladding solutions on the market.

In most houses, the main gate is not the one you use every day. It's the smaller gate — the one on the side, near the backyard, or along a walkway — that actually gets opened again and again.

That's exactly where this 4′ × 6′ gate fits. It's not trying to be big or impressive. It's made for regular use, where things need to work without effort.

Why Size Matters Here

A smaller gate sounds simple, but that's where mistakes usually happen. If the balance is off, even a small gate feels heavy or awkward.

This one sits in that middle zone — not too wide, not too narrow. Enough space to pass comfortably, but not so much that it feels bulky. Because of that, it doesn't demand attention. It just fits in and does its job.

What You Notice First

At first glance, the curved blades stand out — not in a loud way, more like a subtle detail. When light hits the surface, you can see the slight curve creating a soft pattern. It breaks the flatness that most gates have.

It's not decorative in an overdone way. It just gives the gate a bit of character without making it look heavy.

What You Don't Notice (But Matters More)

What really matters shows up after a few days of use — things like:

  • How the gate feels when you open it
  • Whether it aligns properly every time
  • Whether it makes noise or not
  • Whether it feels stable

These are the details people don't think about while buying — but notice later. A gate like this works quietly in the background. No sudden jerks, no dragging feeling, no need to adjust it again and again.

Living With This Gate Daily

This is the kind of gate you stop noticing after a while — and that's actually a good sign. You open it without thinking. Close it without checking twice. It becomes part of your routine.

Whether it's stepping out quickly, letting someone in, or accessing the backyard — it responds the same way every time. That consistency is what makes a gate feel "right."

Material That Doesn't Create Problems Later

A lot of gates feel fine in the beginning but start showing issues after a few months. Here, the material plays a big role. Aluminum behaves differently:

  • It doesn't pick up rust marks
  • It doesn't react badly to moisture
  • It doesn't change shape easily

So instead of slowly degrading, it just stays the same. That means fewer repairs, fewer adjustments, and less thinking about it overall.

Putting It Together Without Overthinking

Installation is usually where things get messy — mismatched parts, extra adjustments, confusion. This kit avoids that. Everything is made to fit together in a straightforward way:

  • Frame connects cleanly
  • Blades sit in place without forcing
  • Hinges align without guesswork

The only thing that really matters is getting the position right. Once that's done, everything else falls into place naturally.

Where It Actually Fits

This gate is not meant for big entrances — and that's exactly why it works well. It fits in places like:

  • Side passages
  • Backyard entries
  • Garden access points
  • Narrow walkways

Anywhere you need a simple entry point that works every day without getting in the way.

Yes, but in a subtle way. It adds depth to the look and avoids the flat, plain feel.

If installed properly, yes. The structure is stable and does not shift easily.

Not at all. Basic cleaning is enough. No repainting or heavy upkeep needed.

Understanding the Gate

This is a wide sliding gate made for entrances where normal gates don't really work well. Instead of opening forward or backward, it moves sideways along a fixed path.

That one change solves a lot of problems — no space blockage, no awkward opening angle, and no struggle when the gate size is large. The 18-foot width handles big driveways easily, while the 6-foot height gives proper coverage without making it feel too closed.

What You Actually Get in This Kit

Instead of selling just a frame, this kit is built as a full system. You get:

  • A strong aluminum frame
  • Sliding track and support system
  • Rollers that carry the weight
  • Stops and guides for control
  • Connectors and hardware

Everything is designed to work together, so you don't have to figure out compatibility on your own. This makes a big difference during installation because random parts usually create problems later.

How the Design Feels in Real Life

On paper, "flat profile design" sounds simple. But in real use, it actually works better than heavy decorative styles. The straight, clean lines don't collect dirt easily, don't feel bulky, and match almost any type of property — modern or basic.

Another important thing is balance. This gate doesn't feel overloaded or too detailed. It looks clean without trying too hard.

Daily Use Experience

This is where most gates fail — not in design, but in daily use. With this sliding system:

  • You don't need to pull hard
  • It doesn't swing into your space
  • It stays controlled while moving
  • It feels predictable every time

Even after repeated use, the movement stays consistent because the weight is supported by rollers instead of hinges. That's what makes it practical — not just good-looking.

Installation Reality

Installation is not complicated, but it needs proper setup. Realistically, the process goes like this:

  1. Prepare the ground and track line
  2. Assemble the frame
  3. Fix the wheels under the gate
  4. Place the gate on the track and align it
  5. Adjust side guides and stops

The most important part is alignment. If that is done right, everything else becomes easy. Because it's a kit, most of the confusion is already removed — you're not building from zero.

Where This Gate Truly Works

This gate works best where:

  • The opening is wide
  • Vehicles move in and out regularly
  • Space in front of the gate is limited
  • A smooth system is needed instead of manual effort

Common places include driveways, villas, commercial entries, and storage or warehouse access. In tight or high-traffic areas, sliding gates simply make more sense than swing gates.

Yes, aluminum does not rust and handles outdoor conditions well, so it stays stable over time.

Not really. Just keep the track clean and check alignment occasionally.

What This Gate Is Really About

This is a 12-foot wide sliding gate designed for medium to large entrances. Instead of opening like a traditional gate, it moves sideways along a fixed path.

That simple change makes a big difference. You don't have to worry about space in front or behind the gate. Everything stays clear, especially useful when cars are moving in and out regularly.

The most noticeable part of this gate is the curved blade design. Instead of flat panels, the blades have a slight curve. This gives the gate a bit of depth and movement when you look at it from different angles. It doesn't feel flat or plain.

At the same time, the design is not overdone. It still looks clean and fits well with modern homes, villas, or even simple properties. It's the kind of design that doesn't try too hard — but still stands out.

Product Overview

The Alu Plexiglass DIY PAD Gate combines an aluminum frame with a Plexiglass infill panel for projects that want enclosure without the visual weight of a fully opaque gate. It is intended as a practical 4×6 pedestrian entry for homeowners, builders, and contractors who want a clean modern appearance and a field-friendly installation process.

Perfect For

Side entrances, courtyards, gardens, backyard access, patios, decks, and light commercial entries where a visually open gate is part of the design.

Built to Last

Side Yards & Courtyards

Create a defined pedestrian entry without turning the passage into a visually heavy privacy wall.

Gardens & Outdoor Living

Pool-area applications require a separate code check. Do not assume the gate is automatically pool-barrier compliant. Gate height, self-closing behavior, latch location, swing direction, openings, mounting conditions, and local code must all be verified for the complete installed assembly.

Design & Durability

Two materials, two jobs: aluminum provides the frame, Plexiglass creates the visual character.

Aluminum Frame

The frame is the structural perimeter of the gate and gives the hinges, latch, and infill a rigid system to work within. Aluminum is naturally resistant to red rust and is well suited to exterior architectural products when properly finished and installed.

The frame uses a powder-coated exterior finish with optional frame colors. Confirm the exact alloy, coating specification, and finish for the ordered configuration before relying on any project-specific compliance requirement.

Plexiglass Infill

The Plexiglass panel is lighter than comparable glass and is used here to maintain visibility and daylight while still creating a physical gate panel. The Plexiglass is intended for exterior use with UV stabilization and impact resistance.

Use mild soap, water, and non-abrasive cleaning materials to reduce scratching and preserve clarity.

Material & Code Note

Do not market the complete Plexiglass gate as an all-aluminum non-combustible assembly.

Important for Zone Zero and wildfire-focused projects

The aluminum frame itself is a non-combustible metal, but Plexiglass is a polymer glazing material. That means this product is materially different from an all-aluminum gate. For projects near structures, in wildfire-prone areas, or where a non-combustible assembly is required, confirm the complete gate configuration with the applicable code, project professional, and authority having jurisdiction before specifying it.

The gate may be DIY-friendly, but the opening still controls the installation.

Before assembly, verify the finished opening, hinge-side structure, swing clearance, latch condition, and level. A clean frame cannot compensate for an opening that is out of square or an unsupported hinge side.

Privacy comes from the profile geometry, not loose boards pushed together.

1. Prepare the Surface

Begin by ensuring that the wall, frame, or structure is clean, level, and structurally sound. Remove any debris, old siding, or protrusions that may affect panel alignment. For exterior applications, especially in areas exposed to heavy rain or high humidity, install a weatherproof sheathing or moisture barrier to protect the underlying structure from water infiltration and extend its lifespan.

2. Measure and Plan Your Layout

Carefully measure the total installation area and mark straight layout lines as your guide. This ensures the panels are perfectly aligned and evenly spaced from start to finish. Decide if you want a horizontal layout for a contemporary look or a vertical arrangement for a classic, elongated appearance. Accurate planning at this stage minimizes cutting waste and ensures a cleaner, faster installation.

3. Install the Starter Strip

Fix a starter strip or base support at the lowest point of the wall or frame, making sure it is level and secure. This strip acts as your anchor, setting the alignment for the first row of panels. A properly installed starter strip is crucial, as even a minor tilt will affect the entire installation.

4. Position and Secure the First Panel

Place the first CLAD120 panel onto the starter strip, aligning it carefully before securing it with corrosion-resistant or stainless-steel screws. The powder-coated aluminum surface is highly durable, but correct screw placement ensures a firm hold and long-term stability.

5. Continue with the Interlocking “Lego-Style” System

Each subsequent panel should slide seamlessly into the groove of the previous one. The precision-engineered interlocking design eliminates visible gaps, locks panels securely in place, and creates a uniform, high-end appearance. This system is not only fast to install but also resistant to warping, shifting, or loosening over time.

6. Trim and Custom Fit as Needed

For openings, corners, and edge transitions, cut the panels with a fine-tooth blade or metal-cutting tools to achieve an exact fit. Always use matching trim accessories to maintain a consistent style and to seal exposed edges against weather exposure.

7. Finish with Cap and Trim Pieces

Complete the installation by adding finishing caps or trim pieces to all open edges. This final step not only enhances visual appeal but also provides added protection against moisture, pests, and UV damage.

Another benefit is adjustability. You can fine-tune the speed and force of the closing action to suit different gate sizes and applications.

After installation, adjust the closer settings to control the speed and force of the gate’s closing action.
